clue.text: Milky white oil's transformed each year in place of independence

indicators.note: something put in place of another takes its spot, so one letter is swapped out for new ones

parts.note: taken as written
PA is per annum, Latin for each year
I is the abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: A recipe or a geology note about milky oil changing year by year somewhere independent.
explanation.walkthrough: In OIL the I is removed and PA takes its place, giving O-PA-L.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone typically showing a milky, pearly whiteness, so its name serves as a colour term.

clue.text: Weak spirit left over weeks in ewers lacks body

indicators.note: the body of a thing is its middle, so lacking it leaves only the outside letters

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
W stands for week, doubled here for the plural, as pp stands for pages
taken as written
the jugs keep only their first and last letters

explanation.surface: A thin drink, left standing for weeks in jugs, has no body to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Low wines are the weak first distillate in whisky-making, before the spirit is run again. 'Weeks' gives two Ws, the plural shown by doubling.
explanation.definitionFit: Distillers call the feeble alcohol from the first still pass by this name before redistilling it into proper whisky.

clue.text: Two teachers picked up rubbish

indicators.note: in a down entry, something picked up is lifted so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: first teacher: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, the teaching degree
second teacher: Sir is how pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: Two teachers collected the rubbish, perhaps on litter duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts as a homophone signal, but in a down clue it lifts each teacher so it reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or broken remains, a close synonym for rubbish lying around.

clue.text: Cuckoo pecked at recorder?

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the following letters go mad and rearrange

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cuckoo pecking at a recorder, the bird or the wooden flute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like the bird doing the pecking, and 'recorder' looks like the flute; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape deck is a machine for playing and capturing sound on magnetic tape, one kind of recording device.

clue.text: Cats touch hearts from time to time

parts.note: tig is the British playground chasing game, and to tig someone is to touch them

indicators.note: something done from time to time happens at intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Cats touching hearts now and then, a sentimental picture of pets.
explanation.walkthrough: Tig (tag in America) is a British children's game where the chaser touches another player.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigers are the largest members of the feline family, so they are big cats.

clue.text: Old impressionist releases second retrospective

indicators.note: a retrospective looks back, so the letters run backwards
releasing a thing lets it go, and second is the usual abbreviation S, so that letter leaves

parts.note: Edgar Degas, French Impressionist painter of ballet dancers

explanation.surface: An old Impressionist painter's retrospective exhibition, releasing a second show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' reads as an art exhibition, fitting the painter, but here it turns DEGA round.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged is an adjective for someone or something advanced in years, a direct synonym.

clue.text: False hope develops around New Year

indicators.note: something that develops grows and changes shape, so the letters are remade with the added ones

parts.note: taken as written
the first letters of New and Year

explanation.surface: False hope building up around New Year resolutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False hope' reads as one phrase; the split falls after 'False'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoney describes something fake or sham, not genuine, matching false as an adjective.

clue.text: Brave call following positive response from Putin?

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece before this word is placed second

to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the call after the Russian yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring is an adjective for someone bold and courageous, ready to take risks, so it matches brave.

clue.text: So blue after first love's gone off the boil

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, and the first one going means it is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
feeling blue is feeling low

explanation.surface: Feeling so sad after a first love affair has cooled off.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is the tennis score zero, the letter O. 'After' only joins the definition to the wordplay, though in the story it reads as a time word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or business off the boil has lost momentum and become sluggish, the idiom for gone slack.

clue.text: Find fault with regularly sharing deeper arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the letters are reordered
regularly means at even intervals, so letters are taken at a fixed step

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Only every other letter of 'sharing' joins the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprehend is a formal verb meaning to rebuke or censure, the same as criticising someone.

clue.text: Uproot and rip out air freshener

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters come out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tearing out an air freshener plug from the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rip out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'rip' is fodder and 'out' alone signals the shuffle; 'and' joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices kept to scent a room pleasantly.

clue.text: Provides continuity in cat broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast goes out over the airwaves, so it is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's continuity announcer bridging programmes, perhaps one about cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continuity' and 'broadcast' both suggest television, where a continuity announcer links shows.
explanation.definitionFit: To link is to connect pieces together, so something that links keeps a sequence unbroken.

clue.text: Fake news about East German subject

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a lie is a falsehood
the first letters of East and German

explanation.surface: Propaganda about an East German topic, a Cold War picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a topic, but it is a person owing allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: Liege can mean a vassal bound to serve a feudal lord, that is, a subject, as well as the lord himself.

clue.text: River estuary flounders — a source of riches for the nation?

definitions.text: a source of riches for the nation?

indicators.note: to flounder is to struggle clumsily, so the letters thrash into a new order

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
taken as written

explanation.surface: Flatfish in a river mouth, the fishing trade being a source of national wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounders' looks like the fish caught in the estuary; it is the verb for struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Treasury is the government department that holds and manages public funds, the state's money store.

clue.text: Regulates decoys changing hands

clue.text: More alternative comedians ultimately follow the French

definitions.note: less is the opposite option to more

parts.note: les is French for the, plural

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: More alternative comedy acts coming after French performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More alternative' reads as more offbeat, like alternative comedy; it means the alternative to 'more'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked whether you want more or fewer, the contrasting choice is this comparative word, its opposite.

clue.text: Slovakia's imprisoning number two spy

indicators.note: to imprison is to shut inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: SK is the international code for Slovakia
number two is a child's euphemism for faeces

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number two' suggests a second-in-command; it is the nursery euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Spook is informal slang for a secret agent or intelligence officer.

clue.text: Talks of speed chess finishing early

indicators.note: finishing early means stopping before the end, so each word's last letter is cut

parts.note: without its final letter
without its final letter

explanation.surface: Talks about rapid chess games that end before time.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words lose their last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeches are formal addresses given to an audience, and a talk is just such an address.

clue.text: Mass rejection of mouthpiece for computers perhaps?

indicators.note: a rejection sends something back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lip, slang for cheeky talk, so a mouthpiece
E for electronic, the prefix used for computer things such as email

explanation.surface: A wholesale rejection of a spokesperson for the computer industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass rejection' reads as one idea; 'Mass' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile is a heap or large accumulated quantity, a common synonym for a mass of things.

clue.text: Iron doesn't begin to support type of rock passage

indicators.note: not beginning means losing the start, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: prog rock, short for progressive rock
to iron is to press, here without its first letter

explanation.surface: Iron bolts that fail to hold up a rock passage, perhaps a tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the pressing comes after the rock genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress means forward movement, as in the progress or passage of time, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Vagrant seen with warm clothing from Savile Row?

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders without a fixed home, so the letters drift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tramp spotted wearing a warm bespoke suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Savile Row is the London street famous for tailoring men's suits, hence the question mark for a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Savile Row tailors make garments for gentlemen, so their output is a sample of male attire.

clue.text: Special Branch's home? Far end of Petticoat Lane

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for special
branches grow on a tree

indicators.note: the far end of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: Where the police Special Branch is based, and the far end of the London market street Petticoat Lane.
explanation.walkthrough: Special Branch is the British police intelligence unit, so this looks like a police address; it splits into Special and Branch. Petticoat Lane is a London street market.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane is a narrow road, and in a town it is simply a kind of road lined with buildings.

clue.text: British team wears no ill-fitting trousers from the East

clue.text: Diver guarding North Dakota's capital

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a loon is a diving bird, the American name for a diver

explanation.definitionFit: London is the seat of government of the United Kingdom, a national capital city.

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the reworked notice behind the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: A direction is an instruction or command, so it is a synonym for an order given.

clue.text: Completely out of order

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about something wholly broken; the two halves are separate meanings.

clue.text: Royal has given up lying — finally? It's true

clue.text: Unlimited trips for section of church

clue.text: Everybody's cribbing the day before examination

clue.text: Henry arises half-cut after stripping down Ford Mustangs?

indicators.note: cutting off half leaves the remaining half, here the back part

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
without its outer letters
the second half of the word

explanation.surface: Henry Ford rising, half-drunk, after taking apart his Mustang cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry and Ford point to the car maker and Mustang to its car; 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk. The question mark flags mustangs as one example of the answer.
